headline_hook: Samsung Holds Health Data Hostage While Hebbia Bets Finance on Claude
preview_topics: llama.cpp runs Hunyuan locally with speculative decoding

pick_of_the_day.thesis: Samsung's delete-or-consent ultimatum isn't just bad UX — it's the first major test of whether health-data regulators will treat AI training consent the same way they treat medical consent, and the answer will set the template for every fitness and wellness app that follows.

model_literacy.relevance: llama.cpp's new Hy3 support uses multi-token prediction speculative decoding to run massive MoE models locally — a draft model proposes several tokens at once and the main model verifies them in a single forward pass, trading a little memory for dramatically faster inference. This is why architectures that were cloud-only months ago are now running on local hardware.

items.title: Hebbia Shows What 'Can't Miss a Detail' Actually Means for Frontier AI in Finance
items.angle: Not another chatbot wrapper — Hebbia is using Claude for financial due diligence where a single missed clause costs millions, and Anthropic is publishing the playbook.
items.key_fact: Anthropic case study details how Hebbia automates financial diligence workflows where exhaustive document coverage is a legal requirement, not a nice-to-have.

items.title: Samsung Tells Health App Users: Let Us Train AI on Your Data or We Delete It
items.angle: A coercive consent pattern in health data that will force regulators to draw a line — and set a precedent every wellness app will either follow or be measured against.
items.key_fact: Samsung Health users who opt out of AI training consent are told their stored health data will be deleted.

items.title: llama.cpp Cracks Open Hunyuan V3 with Multi-Token Speculative Decoding
items.angle: Tencent's massive MoE architecture now runs locally — and the speculative decoding support means it's actually fast enough to be usable.
items.key_fact: Release b9993 adds Hy3 (HunyuanV3) architecture support with MTP speculative decoding; b9990 adds Minimax2 eagle3 spec decoding; b9992 refactors CUDA MMQ kernels for Blackwell GPUs.

items.title: Qwythos 9B Hits 45K Downloads as Local Multimodal Converges on the Sweet Spot
items.angle: Another data point that the 7–9B parameter range is becoming the standard for local multimodal inference.
items.key_fact: 9B multimodal image-text-to-text model in GGUF format with 45.2K downloads and 102 likes on HuggingFace.

items.title: MCP TypeScript SDK Splits Its Core for the 2.0 Era
items.angle: If you're building MCP servers, your imports are about to break — schemas and protocol constants now live in @modelcontextprotocol/core.
items.key_fact: Spec schemas, OAuth schemas, and protocol constants extracted to a shared @modelcontextprotocol/core package in v2.0.0-beta.4.

items.title: Vercel AI SDK Ships Four Patches in Three Days, Fixes a Streaming Memory Leak
items.angle: The v7.0.25 fix for cancelled transcription streams not aborting pending connections is the kind of silent leak that eats your serverless budget.
items.key_fact: v7.0.25 fixes a streaming transcription memory leak where cancelled streams didn't abort pending connections; v7.0.26 groups orphaned tool calls under parent spans.

items.title: Next.js 16.3 Preview Graduates Request Insights, Fixes Turbopack CSS Ordering
items.angle: The CSS Modules ordering fix for Turbopack resolves a real pain point — styles that worked in webpack were breaking in Turbopack builds.
items.key_fact: Request Insights graduates from canary to preview; Turbopack fix orders CSS modules by chunk-group co-occurrence.

items.title: Jacquard: A Language Designed from Scratch for AI-Written, Human-Reviewed Code
items.angle: The bet that existing languages weren't designed for the AI-writes-human-reviews workflow — worth watching whether purpose-built wins or better tooling for existing languages does.
items.key_fact: New programming language explicitly designed for the AI-generation, human-review workflow pattern.

items.title: Academic Study Examines How Microsoft Deployed Claude Code Alongside Copilot CLI
items.angle: Rare empirical data on how a major tech company evaluates competing AI coding tools internally — not a benchmark, but a real deployment study.
items.key_fact: Academic paper examines Microsoft's early 2026 internal rollout of Claude Code alongside GitHub Copilot CLI.

items.title: MIT Finds a Way to Audit AI Training Data for CSAM Without Generating Any
items.angle: A significant advance in AI safety auditing that solves the ethical paradox of verification — you can now check without reproducing the harm.
items.key_fact: MIT technique detects whether models were trained on child abuse material without generating any harmful content during the audit.

items.title: Someone Built a Working Neural Network in Pure SQL
items.angle: More interesting as a proof of SQL's computational completeness than a production pattern — but a reminder that your database can do more than you think.
items.key_fact: Fully working neural network implementation using only SQL operations, demonstrated on MNIST.

items.title: The Practical Guide to Running RL Training at 4-Bit NVFP4 Precision
items.angle: Documents the exact stability–performance tradeoffs teams hit when pushing RL onto consumer GPUs with aggressive quantization.
items.key_fact: Detailed guide to NVFP4 4-bit precision reinforcement learning, covering stability tradeoffs on consumer hardware.

items.title: DOOMQL: Yes, Someone Ran DOOM Through a Query Language
items.angle: When Simon Willison covers a 'run DOOM in X' project, there's usually a genuine technical insight hiding under the fun.
items.key_fact: DOOM running through query-language mechanics, highlighted by Simon Willison.

items.title: vox-director: An Agent That Turns a Topic into a Finished Vox-Style Explainer Video
items.angle: One of the more complete open-source automated video production pipelines — topic in, finished paper-collage explainer video out.
items.key_fact: End-to-end agent pipeline producing Vox-style explainer videos using Atlas Cloud + ffmpeg, 103 GitHub stars.

quick_links.title: headroom: Track Claude & Codex Usage Across Accounts Without Spending Tokens
quick_links.angle: Live dashboard for teams managing multiple AI coding subscriptions.
quick_links.key_fact: 73 GitHub stars; monitors Claude and Codex usage across multiple accounts.

quick_links.title: Lorde Calls Ray-Ban Meta AI Glasses 'Not Sexy' at Their Own Sponsored Festival
quick_links.angle: Cultural backlash from a high-profile artist signals adoption headwinds for AI wearables.
quick_links.key_fact: Public criticism at a Ray-Ban-sponsored festival event.

quick_links.title: BillAI Bass: AWS Strands Agents Wired to a Big Mouth Billy Bass
quick_links.angle: A clean reference implementation for connecting agentic AI to physical hardware.
quick_links.key_fact: 52 HN upvotes; uses AWS Strands Agents framework for IoT integration.

quick_links.title: Claude as Mr. Meeseeks: Spawn an Agent, Do the Job, Vanish
quick_links.angle: Ephemeral agent design pattern wrapped in a perfect metaphor.
quick_links.key_fact: 87 HN upvotes; reframes Claude Code agents as single-purpose Meeseeks.
